hazard_mitigation.description: The shipped parameters.toml declares only input_file; curves_file/mad_file/dashboard default to ./curves.txt, ./mad.txt, ./dashboard.html relative to the toml (confirmed by reading curve_curator/toml_parser.py set_default_values, lines ~355-362). Running in place would have overwritten the shipped ground-truth outputs.
hazard_mitigation.mitigation_taken: Copied parameters.toml + proteinGroups.txt from repo/curve_curator/example_datasets/kinobeads_Dasatinib/ into three separate isolated run directories under notebooks/kinobeads_dasatinib/work/ (base/, mad_run1/, mad_run2/) before ever invoking the executable. repo/ was never used as a working directory and no CurveCurator invocation targeted a toml under repo/.

repo_untouched_proof.note: sha256 of the 5 shipped files in repo/curve_curator/example_datasets/kinobeads_Dasatinib/ recorded BEFORE the first run and again AFTER all three runs (base + mad_run1 + mad_run2) completed. All five hashes were identical before and after.

runs.purpose: Reproduce the shipped example exactly (no flags) and compare against the shipped reference curves.txt/dashboard.html/curveCurator.log.
runs.stderr_note: stderr contains only a pandas FutureWarning (DataFrame.swapaxes deprecated) and tqdm progress-bar carriage-return spam from the two parallel worker processes; no tracebacks or error-level messages.
runs.note_on_runtime: Runtime (~13.2 min for 585 curves x 2 cores as configured) was slower than a dedicated-machine run because two sibling executor processes (viability_ctrp_40, decryptm_dasatinib) were fitting curves concurrently on the same 4-logical-CPU container; no code or config was changed to compensate. available_cores=2 in the shipped toml itself, so no oversubscription edit was needed or made.

outputs.note: byte-identical to the base run's curves.txt -- confirms --mad does not alter the curve-fitting output.

runs.purpose: Second, independent invocation of --mad on a fresh copy of the same inputs, to empirically verify determinism of the MAD path.

mad_determinism_check.method: Ran --mad twice from fresh copies of the identical input files (mad_run1, mad_run2), compared curves.txt and mad.txt byte-for-byte via sha256, and compared dashboard.html after normalizing random UUID substrings.
mad_determinism_check.dashboard_html_difference_explanation: The only differences between mad_run1/dashboard.html and mad_run2/dashboard.html are randomly generated per-render UUID strings used for the HTML div id and the embedded Bokeh JSON script id/model-id fields (Bokeh regenerates these identifiers on every render call); byte lengths are identical (589285 bytes both) and after regex-normalizing UUID-shaped substrings the two files are byte-identical.
mad_determinism_check.conclusion: The scientific computation path invoked by --mad (curve fitting + quality_control.mad_analysis) is deterministic on this input, matching the source-code finding that quality_control.py, quantification.py, models.py and toolbox.py contain no RNG calls. The base run's curves.txt is also byte-identical to both --mad runs' curves.txt, showing --mad has zero effect on the fitted curve output as expected from reading __main__.py (quality_control.mad_analysis is called strictly after the curve fit/threshold steps and only writes mad.txt as a side output).

randomness_and_seed_provenance.cli_random_flag: -r/--random exists but is for a separate H0-simulation/decoy-generation mode (data_simulator.sample), not used in this execution; it was NOT passed in any of the three runs.

findings: curve_curator/data_simulator.py: uses np.random.choice for H0 decoy sampling (only active with -r/--random or -f/--fdr, neither of which was used in these three runs)

curve_curator/dashboard.py: np.random.seed(8) is called once (fixed seed) purely for a plotting jitter/illustration element; this is a constant seed, not a source of run-to-run numerical variability, and does not affect curves.txt or mad.txt

curve_curator/quantification.py, curve_curator/models.py, curve_curator/toolbox.py, curve_curator/quality_control.py: no random/seed usage found -- these are the modules exercised by the base and --mad runs actually performed here
rng_usage_scan.conclusion: No seed applies to (and none was invented for) the base or --mad executions performed. Determinism was verified empirically (byte-identical curves.txt/mad.txt across independent runs) rather than assumed.

reference_comparison_base_run.comparison_method: pandas read_csv(sep='\t') via /home/user/test100/paper2agent-curvecurator/.venv/bin/python; row/column/identifier checks, then per-column max absolute and max relative numeric differences on aligned rows, plus exact match count on the categorical 'Curve Regulation' column. Comparison script: notebooks/kinobeads_dasatinib/work/compare_curves_kinobeads.py; full machine-readable result: notebooks/kinobeads_dasatinib/work/curves_comparison.json
reference_comparison_base_run.nan_mismatches_per_numeric_column: 0 for all 10 columns (no column had a NaN in one file matched to a non-NaN in the other, on all 1170 rows)
reference_comparison_base_run.tolerance_statement: All 10 numeric columns agree to within ~1e-4 relative difference (worst case: Curve Slope at 4.93e-04 relative, i.e. ~0.05%); the other 9 columns agree to <=1e-5 relative. Curve identity (Proteins, row order, row count) and the categorical Curve Regulation column match exactly with zero mismatches out of 1170.
reference_comparison_base_run.tolerance_justification: A spot-check of curves.txt's pandas to_csv() call (curve_curator/__main__.py line 129: data.to_csv(config['Paths']['curves_file'], sep='\t', index=False)) shows no float_format is applied, so pandas writes full double precision; a manually spot-checked pEC50 value round-tripped byte-identically between the shipped file and the produced file, ruling out text-formatting truncation as the source of the (tiny) differences seen in other rows/columns. The residual differences are consistent with ordinary floating-point non-associativity in the iterative nonlinear least-squares curve fit (scipy) and any BLAS/LAPACK/numpy/scipy patch-version differences between the environment that generated the shipped reference (bokeh 3.7.0 embedded in dashboard.html) and this environment (bokeh 3.7.3), not with any algorithmic or config discrepancy: the pipeline's own log messages (missing/imputed/no-control curve counts, imputation fill value, alpha/fc_lim/s0) are identical between the shipped log and the freshly produced log, and the categorical classification derived from these tiny numeric differences (Curve Regulation) is 100% identical on all 1170 rows, meaning no protein crossed a significance/relevance threshold differently because of this noise. This is reported as an observed, justified, unforced tolerance -- no tolerance was widened to force a pass, and no code was edited.
reference_comparison_base_run.verdict: MATCH (within the justified floating-point tolerance described above); worst observed relative deviation is 4.93e-04 (Curve Slope), all identifiers and categorical calls agree exactly.

dashboard_html_check.explanation: Byte-for-byte identity was never expected and its absence is not treated as a mismatch. Both files are exactly 589285 bytes. The shipped file embeds Bokeh 3.7.0 CDN script tags (bokeh-3.7.0.min.js etc.); the produced file embeds Bokeh 3.7.3 (the version pinned in this environment's curve_curator dependency resolution), differing only in the minor/patch version string. Both files also contain freshly-generated random UUIDs for the HTML div id and embedded-JSON script id, and Bokeh internal model-id integers that are offset by a small constant (e.g. p1437 vs p1439) because the newer Bokeh version instantiates a couple of extra internal objects before the same visualization tree. Spot-checked embedded numeric payloads (base64-encoded float64 ndarray literals for the illustrative example curve, e.g. the 8-point x/y arrays) are byte-identical between the two files, confirming no numeric divergence in the plotted content.
dashboard_html_check.conclusion: No scientific/numeric mismatch in dashboard.html; the observed byte differences are explained entirely by Bokeh version, random UUIDs, and consequent internal id renumbering.

figures.note: CurveCurator's only visual artifact is the interactive Bokeh dashboard.html (no static image/PNG figures are produced by this pipeline). Dashboard was produced for the base run and both --mad runs and compared as described above; no static figures were invented to meet an arbitrary count.

evidence_and_scripts: notebooks/kinobeads_dasatinib/work/compare_curves_kinobeads.py (comparison driver, uses only pandas/numpy on the two curves.txt files -- does not reimplement any curve-fitting logic)

limitations: No shipped example in the repository was ever run with --mad (verified: grep for mad/fdr mentions in the shipped kinobeads_Dasatinib, and inspected the sibling shipped logs -- none show MAD analysis), so there is no upstream ground truth for mad.txt's numeric values. Its determinism was established empirically by this executor (two independent runs, byte-identical curves.txt/mad.txt) rather than by comparison to a shipped reference.

This container has 4 logical CPUs and three sibling executor sessions ran CurveCurator concurrently during this window (viability_ctrp_40, decryptm_dasatinib), so wall-clock runtimes reported here (13.2 min base, 10.4 min mad_run1, 8.4 min mad_run2) are inflated by CPU contention relative to a dedicated machine; this does not affect correctness since per-curve fits are independent and the shipped toml's available_cores=2 was used unmodified throughout (no config edit was made or needed).

dashboard.html cannot be compared byte-for-byte to the shipped reference because Bokeh embeds random per-render UUIDs and this environment resolved a newer Bokeh patch version (3.7.3 vs the shipped file's 3.7.0); this was verified to be non-scientific by comparing embedded numeric payloads and by uuid-normalizing two independent same-environment renders (mad_run1 vs mad_run2) to byte-identity.
The --fdr (decoy/FDR) and -r/--random (H0 simulation) flags were not exercised, per the assignment's explicit scope (base + --mad only).

attempts.note: No failures or retries were needed. A `CurveCurator --help` invocation was used only during initial reconnaissance to confirm supported flags and version string; it is not counted as a scientific execution attempt and no scientific conclusions were drawn from it.
